\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood estimates of the change in an app's Indian-language reviews after its AI launch, relative to its English reviews in the same month. The first row reports $100[\exp(\hat\beta)-1]$ percent, where $\hat\beta$ is the coefficient on AI launch $\times$ Indian language. Standard errors in brackets are delta-method transformations of standard errors clustered by app; the confidence interval transforms the 95\% interval for $\hat\beta$. All columns include app $\times$ month, language $\times$ month and app $\times$ language fixed effects. Observations are app $\times$ language $\times$ month cells, after dropping groups with no reviews. Language measures: (1) reviews mixing English with a few Indian-language words count as English; (2) they count as Indian-language; (3) only reviews in an Indian script count as Indian-language; (4) Google Play's language tag. Randomization inference: share of 1,000 placebo estimates (random apps and launch months) at least as large in absolute value as the estimate in column (1).
\end{tablenotes}
